title: Empirica run-scoped Docker spike qualification record /3
description: The closed shape of siffran.empirica.docker-spike-qualification-record/3 (Empirica 7.2 section 4.5), written durably and content-addressed under $EMPIRICA_SANDBOX_HOME/docker-spike-qualification-v3/records/ before the run's binding compare-and-set (write-first). This schema is the record shape's definition home; the runtime validator (adapters/sandbox/run_qualification.py:validate_run_record) remains the authoritative admission and is registered with the ADR-0075 contract conformance harness: its x-core-ingress declares the record root, every definition it reaches names its own shape callable under x-core-validator, and core.contract_registry carries the core's own declaration of the same keys, so the harness's differential holds the closed shapes (never hand-written test-side restatements). The runtime admission (adapters/sandbox/run_qualification.py:validate_run_record) remains the authoritative gate: it composes on the annotated shape callables and owns the semantic rules this schema cannot express, which stay behaviour-tested by named owner tests: the /2 runtime and daemon-identity admission, the semantic-authority projection and its digest, the exact policy, implementation and probe-image identity bindings, the platform cross-field identities, the UTF-8 byte bound on identifiers, the probe order and expected/observed equality, the execution_binding_digest recomputation, the run-generation lineage on load, the /2 namespace isolation, and the exact content-addressed file name and qualification_record_digest equality.

runtime.description: The observed Docker runtime facts of the pinned daemon, exactly the /2 runtime shape (docker_cli, endpoint, context, versions, platforms, security options, resource-limit capability flags, capacity, host facts, discovery_reads, optional daemon_id). The closed field set and the capability admission are the /2 authority contract's; they are not restated here. The full server_version stays a diagnostic of these facts: the execution binding (recomputed by the runtime admission) binds only its major part, and within one qualification attempt the exact version must still match.

semantic_authority.description: The canonical semantic projection of the runtime (endpoint, platform, required security, resource-limit capability flags, optional daemon_id); equal to the bound authority up to the documented daemon_id rule.

daemon_id.description: Docker info.ID when the observed daemon reports one; present exactly when the runtime carries it, and equal to it.

digest.description: The one digest lexeme; the absolute end anchor, never a bare $ (which Python matches before a trailing line feed), keeps both judges in agreement with core.freshness.

identifier.description: One closed identifier lexeme; the runtime admission's byte bound (128 UTF-8 bytes) is semantic on top, never expressible here.

x-core-only.rule: A JSON integer member lands as a Python int in the core, never a float with a zeroed fraction (draft 2020-12 admits 2.0 for an integer) — the schema cannot say which Python class a number arrives as.

id.description: The full daemon image ID observed at qualification: a diagnostic, never a spike admission gate. The row is inspected, never probed, and carries no capability list; a later per-spike resolution compares this stored ID, it never re-derives it from a re-observed image (spike images may be rebuilt without requalifying).

declared_volumes.description: An image that declares volumes is not admissible: the row is sealed only with none.

x-core-only.rule: A JSON integer member lands as a Python int in the core, never a float with a zeroed fraction (draft 2020-12 admits 2.0 for an integer) — the schema cannot say which Python class a number arrives as.

elapsedMs.description: The record's elapsed milliseconds: zero to the 90 s default qualification budget made exclusive on its last millisecond (the engines draw inclusive maxima), set from the operator timing session's measured evidence; the owner constant DEFAULT_QUALIFICATION_SECONDS owns the binding code-side and re-measuring the timing session may move it.

spikeImages.description: The environment proposal's 1..16 approved local references, each sealed to its daemon image ID and canonical server-native platform with no declared volumes (Empirica 7.2 section 4.1). The rows carry no capability list, because spike images are inspected, never probed (Empirica 7.2 section 4.5); the shared qualification-image helper keeps its own list for the one trusted probe image. Per-spike resolution — and the platform re-verification it repeats under the pinned endpoint — is E10's, not this record's.

x-core-only.rule: A JSON integer member lands as a Python int in the core, never a float with a zeroed fraction (draft 2020-12 admits 2.0 for an integer) — the schema cannot say which Python class a number arrives as.

realization_digest.description: The container's observed top-level Image realization digest on verdict probes; an unavailable probe admits no result, so it records none.
